identity: Dawnmere feeds the road to Highcourt, but boars, rats and a remarkably confused requisition gang are eating the harvest first.

quests.title: Eight Snouts Too Many
quests.text: Barley Piglets are eating next winter's bread before we've had a chance to bake it. Hunt eight by day in the {name:home_fields}, which lie {zone_area:home_fields}. They leave you alone until you strike, so you choose the quarrel; just don't choose three at once.

variants.text: A pit prop ought to hold up a mine, not feed a pig. Hunt eight Pine Piglets by day in the {name:timberline}, which lies {zone_area:timberline}, before they root through another stack. They won't start the fight, so for once in Hearthpine somebody other than me decides when the shift begins.

We planted those saplings for children yet unborn; the Glade Piglets consider them breakfast. Cull eight by day in the {name:home_glades}, which lie {zone_area:home_glades}. They will let you strike first, which is more patience than they have ever shown a seedling.

Water carried home on tired shoulders should reach a mouth, not leak from a chewed waterskin. Hunt eight Scrub Piglets by day in the {name:wellfields}, which lie {zone_area:wellfields}. They wait for you to strike first, and an orc who is handed the first blow does not waste it.

A root feeds a troll, a troll tends the root; the Yam Piglets have eaten their way into the middle of that song. Hunt eight by day in the {name:yam_beds}, which lie {zone_area:yam_beds}. They leave you be until you strike, so take them one verse at a time.

The Barrow Piglets have been rearranging people I buried with considerable care. Kill eight by day in the {name:dead_furrows}, which lie {zone_area:dead_furrows}. They will wait for you to strike, which is more consideration than they show the residents.

quests.lesson: First hunt by day, offered at once with the night's rats; the early potion choice.

quests.title: The Rats Can Mend It
quests.text: The Barn Rats have eaten my grain and left me a sack that holds nothing but a grudge. Kill three after dark in the {name:home_fields}, which lie {zone_area:home_fields}, or farther out in the {name:meadows}, and bring me one Rat Fur Patch. They bite before they ask, and patching rat holes with rat fur is what I call good housekeeping.

variants.text: Something's been at my flour sacks after the late shift, and for once it isn't a miner. Kill three Timber Rats after dark in the {name:timberline}, which lies {zone_area:timberline}, and bring me one Rat Fur Patch. They bite first and never apologise; I'll do the stitching, since every miner in this hall mends a sack with nails.

Three generations of careful weaving, and the Fern Rats decide my seed baskets need doors. Kill three after dark in the {name:home_glades}, which lie {zone_area:home_glades}, and bring me one Rat Fur Patch. I can mend a basket, but teaching manners to its visitors has proved a longer undertaking.

Dust Rats have chewed through my food sacks and dragged the scraps off to line their beds. Kill three after dark in the {name:wellfields}, which lie {zone_area:wellfields}, and bring me one Rat Fur Patch. They charge on sight, so meet them head-on; they slept on my supper, they can patch my sacks.

My yam sacks have more holes than sack, and the Moss Rats look suspiciously well fed. Kill three after dark in the {name:yam_beds}, which lie {zone_area:yam_beds}, and bring me one Rat Fur Patch. They made the holes, so it's only fair they lend a little of themselves to the mending.

Our shroud sacks have begun returning their contents to the floor, courtesy of the Grave Rats. Kill three after dark in the {name:dead_furrows}, which lie {zone_area:dead_furrows}, and bring me one Rat Fur Patch. Death is no excuse for untidy storage.

quests.lesson: Night target at a third of the day count (one night suffices); ordinary loot has uses.

quests.title: A Useful Weight
quests.text: A gap in a wall is an invitation, and Dawnmere has quite enough guests with tusks. Bring me ten blocks of stone, any kind, for the repairs. If you need to gather some, a Wooden Pickaxe will loosen ordinary rock outside town.

variants.text: Good masonry starts with sound stone and someone willing to carry it. Bring me ten blocks of stone, any kind, for our walls. A Wooden Pickaxe will get you started on ordinary rock outside town; I promise not to judge the load by how loudly you put it down.

The low walls keep wandering feet away from our youngest roots. Bring me ten blocks of stone, any kind, to mend the gaps. A Wooden Pickaxe can gather ordinary rock outside town; even a garden meant to outlast us needs work today.

A wall with a gap is just a heap of stone making promises. Bring me ten blocks of stone, any kind, and we will make ours useful again. If your pack is empty, take a Wooden Pickaxe to ordinary rock outside town.

Rain finds every loose stone in a wall, and then it invites the mud indoors. Bring me ten blocks of stone, any kind, for the repairs. A Wooden Pickaxe will gather ordinary rock outside town; moss makes every rock look friendly, but only some of them mean it.

Our walls are losing stones, and I would like to catch the habit before it spreads to the residents. Bring me ten blocks of stone, any kind. A Wooden Pickaxe will gather ordinary rock outside town; if it has a name and two dates on it, choose another rock.

quests.lesson: Craft a Wooden Pickaxe to dig stone; the reward is the next tools, never the request.

quests.title: The Fire Eats Too
quests.text: An oven full of good intentions still serves a cold dinner. Bring me five logs of any tree and five Coal Lumps; you can gather the logs and mine the coal outside town. Whole logs, please, not planks, and leave Dawnmere's trees standing.

variants.text: Every mouth in Hearthpine wants supper, including the smokehouse. Bring me five logs of any tree and five Coal Lumps; the woods and rock outside town can supply both. Logs, mind, not planks, and leave the town trees alone or Brunna will have words with us both.

Saelin can warm a gathering with a speech; I have tried it on the oven without success. Bring me five logs of any tree and five Coal Lumps, gathered outside town if you need them. Leave our planted trees standing, and keep the logs whole; supper has waited quite long enough for eloquence.

My grandmother's grandmother tended the Long Fire, and every cook since has kept it fed. Bring me five whole logs of any tree and five Coal Lumps from the trees and rock outside town; Sunscar's own trees stay standing. One day you can tell your grandchildren you fed the Long Fire, and leave out how often I had to ask.

Rain drums on my roof, hungry trolls drum on my table, and the oven contributes nothing at all. Bring me five whole logs of any tree and five Coal Lumps from outside town. Leave Kapok's trees standing, unless you plan to hold up our shade yourself.

The fire beneath my brine pot has gone out, and glaring at it has achieved very little. Bring me five whole logs of any tree and five Coal Lumps; gather them outside Stillgrave's warded ground if you need to. Leave the town trees standing; some of us have grown rather attached to their shade.

quests.lesson: Any log counts, coal from the rock; town plants are protected.

quests.title: Room at the Table
quests.text: The hands that bring in our harvest deserve more than a crust at the end of the day. Bring me ten pieces of Raw Meat for the kitchen; anything already in your pack is welcome. Heroes run on supper too, whatever the songs say.

variants.text: When the snow shuts us in, I mean to hear snoring, not stomachs. Bring me ten pieces of Raw Meat for the winter racks; anything you've saved will do. A cellar doesn't fill itself while we admire the mountain.
The planting crews eat last and pretend they are not hungry. Bring me ten pieces of Raw Meat; what you have already set aside is welcome. I mean to have supper waiting before anyone has to pretend.

Hear those stomachs trying to drown out the hunters' stories? Bring me ten pieces of Raw Meat for the pot; I can use what is already in your pack. There is room at this fire for quiet folk as well as loud ones.

Everyone has a cousin coming to supper, and somehow the cousins all have cousins. Bring me ten pieces of Raw Meat; anything you have saved will help. I have counted the bowls twice and decided to stop counting people.

A mourner may insist they cannot face a meal, but I still leave a bowl within reach. Bring me ten pieces of Raw Meat for the kitchen; anything already in your pack is welcome. An empty chair is sorrow enough without an empty table.

quests.lesson: Hunt loot is useful; raw food cooks in the oven.

quests.title: Metal for the Mending
quests.text: Every loose hinge in Dawnmere seems to find its way onto my list. Bring me three Copper Bars and three Tin Bars for the town repairs. If you need to make them, smelt the local copper and tin ore in a furnace; a door that closes will spare me several complaints.

variants.text: A shaft prop is only as trustworthy as its fittings, and miners put their lives beneath ours. Bring me three Copper Bars and three Tin Bars for the repairs. You can smelt the local copper and tin ore in a furnace; I can work with a crooked bar, but not an empty promise.

Our hall has heard a great deal of wisdom; lately its hinges insist on answering back. Bring me three Copper Bars and three Tin Bars for the repairs. You can smelt the local copper and tin ore in a furnace, and with luck the next voice raised in that hall will be someone's, not something's.

A loose fitting at the well wastes water every time someone hauls a bucket. Bring me three Copper Bars and three Tin Bars for repairs. A furnace will smelt the local copper and tin ore if you need supplies; no one should carry a full bucket's weight for half a drink.

The rain has been testing our fittings, and some have answered by falling off. Bring me three Copper Bars and three Tin Bars for repairs. You can smelt the local copper and tin ore in a furnace; I would rather hear hammers than another door landing in the mud.

The hinges on our storage chests groan every time I lift a lid, and around here groaning is a privilege of the residents. Bring me three Copper Bars and three Tin Bars for repairs. You can smelt the local copper and tin ore in a furnace; I would like the chests to rest as quietly as everyone else.

quests.lesson: Ore to bar in a Furnace; the Dual Furnace makes the first alloy.

quests.title: A Little Bronze Goes Far
quests.text: Dawnmere wears out tools faster than I can count them, and someone has been using my best hammer as a fence post. Bring me three Bronze Bars for the workshop. If you make them yourself, a Dual Furnace will alloy Copper Bars and Tin Bars into bronze.

variants.text: The mountain has plenty left to give, and our workshop has plenty left to mend. Bring me three Bronze Bars. A Dual Furnace can alloy copper and tin if you're making your own; bring the metal, and I'll supply the opinions on workmanship.

Copper and tin each have their virtues; put them together and you gain a third, which is more than most councils manage. Bring me three Bronze Bars for the workshop. A Dual Furnace will alloy Copper Bars and Tin Bars if you wish to make them yourself; a good tool, like a good tree, repays patience.

The clan needs sound metal for tools, and the workshop cannot hammer boasts into shape. Bring me three Bronze Bars. A Dual Furnace can alloy copper and tin if you want to make your own; the smith will be glad of something solid to work with.

Everyone borrows the village tools, but few remember that the tools need tending too. Bring me three Bronze Bars for the workshop. If you make them yourself, a Dual Furnace can alloy copper and tin, two voices sharing a fire without trying to sing over each other.

A workshop needs fresh metal even when most of its customers have stopped growing. Bring me three Bronze Bars for the tools we mend. A Dual Furnace can alloy copper and tin if you wish to make them yourself; happily, the metals get along better than most families at a reading of the will.

quests.lesson: Alloys in the Dual Furnace; the Bronze Pickaxe digs Iron.

quests.title: Foxes at Our Expense
quests.text: Our hens have taken to sleeping with one eye open, and now the farmers are doing it too. Hunt eight Henthieves by day in the {name:pastures}, which lie {zone_area:pastures}; they wait for your first blow, but the Grunters rooting among them will not. A hen ought to be able to cross her own yard without ending up as someone else's supper.

variants.text: Every spring we sow for a forest; every spring the foxes discover our generosity. Cull eight Russet Kits by day in the {name:foxglades}, which lie {zone_area:foxglades}, and mind the Acorn Grunters that share them. I have time to plant again, but the seedlings have only the roots they stand on.

quests.lesson: A day hunt; the level-5 chest armor choice (one enchant).

quests.title: Claws on the Shore
quests.text: The fishermen came back with torn nets and some very firm opinions about Wreck Snappers. Kill five by day on the {name:wreck_coast}, {dir_from_giver:wreck_coast}; they come at you on sight. Go while the sun is up, because after dark the drowned walk that shore, and I would rather you came home for supper.

variants.text: Boulder Crabs have been taking bites out of our shore gear, and I refuse to put 'digested' in the repair book again. Kill five by day among the {name:rockpools}, {dir_from_giver:rockpools}. Keep room to move; anything that cracks timber deserves more respect than a wet boot.

quests.lesson: A scarce shore target by day; the level-8 legs armor choice (one enchant).

quests.title: A Brush and a Better Supper
quests.text: I have a flour shelf to dust and a supper to rescue. Bring me two Crab Legs from the Wreck Snappers on the {name:wreck_coast}, {dir_from_giver:wreck_coast}, and one Fox Tail from the Henthieves in the {name:pastures}, which lie {zone_area:pastures}; hunt both by day. Legs for the pot, tail for the shelf, and do try to keep them in separate pockets.
quests.lesson: Keep what your enchants need, hand in what they do not.

quests.title: Requisition for One Crumb
quests.text: {name:confused_bandit_chief} calls our missing grain a requisition, though he cannot say who requisitioned it. Defeat seven Grain Pilferers and their chief at the {name:bandit_camp}, {dir_from_giver:bandit_camp}; they keep their posts day and night. We planted that harvest, and a man with a stolen sack and a long word does not get to decide who eats it.
quests.completion: Crumb has filed his last requisition, and the grain stays with the hands that grew it. You've done right by Dawnmere; when you take to the road, you'll carry more good wishes than your pack has room for.
quests.lesson: A camp pack plus a named leader; the weapon choice (prefix and suffix).

quests.title: The Next Sack of Grain
quests.text: Crumb's accounts point to more missing grain in Goldmead Vale; this reaches beyond our fields. Follow the road into the vale and tell Marta Millward in Goldmead Village what happened here. Finish your preparations before you go, and remember that a full pack beats a brave speech on a long road.
quests.lesson: Start zone to home zone handoff.
